thread:
jess-support: customer reports SSE stream (EventSource) from /v1/streams stops emitting after ~10s in Safari only. Works in Chrome. They see partial payloads then no more events, connection stays open. Customer says the page uses <link rel="prefetch"> for next route. headers they sent: Authorization: Bearer <token>, Cache-Control: max-age=0, Accept: text/event-stream. They saw CloudFront return a 304 once before stall. Asking for triage.
sam-frontend: can you paste a minimal repro? do they use a polyfill EventSource or native? safari version?
jess-support: Safari 15.4 macOS, native EventSource. customer tried with our polyfill too, same result. Quick curl against the endpoint works and streams fine on our side. They attached a HAR but redacted token.
kai-qa: I reproduced locally by adding a <link rel="prefetch" href="/next-route"> on a test app. In Safari the prefetch seems to open a speculative request which triggers the CDN to serve a 304 on the actual EventSource request path (edge key mismatch). After the 304 we get no chunked frames for a while, client sees no events even though server is still writing. Console shows no CORS errors.
sam-frontend: Safari prefetch behavior is weird w/ Authorization header — prefetch may not include credentials which can make the edge treat requests as different and cause a cache hit/miss flip. Two quick checks: does the SSE route set Vary: Authorization and Cache-Control: no-transform,no-cache? also ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is present.
leo-eng-sre: looking at recent infra changes: deploy-bot rolled a cache rule on 2026-03-10 that allows edge to answer 304 for certain query params. If the edge returns 304 for a streaming endpoint, some browsers (Safari) expect a full response and then stall when no further chunks arrive. Recommend preventing CDN from returning 304 for SSE endpoints.
jess-support: action items for customer asked: 1) reproduce with prefetch removed, 2) capture server request_id from our logs (we need request-id header), 3) sample curl with -v to show response headers. they said they'd test removing prefetch.
kai-qa: mitigation for now: add response headers on the SSE endpoint: Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform, Connection: keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no (nginx) and Surrogate-Control: no-store (if using CDN). Also ensure your CDN rule bypasses caching for paths matching /v1/streams and does not normalize Authorization away.
sam-frontend: add a small keepalive ping payload from server every 10s: send ":keepalive\n\n" or a comment line so the eventsource won't be considered idle by any intermediary.
leo-eng-sre: we'll add a short-term edge rule to ignore 304s on /v1/streams and set origin to return explicit Cache-Control. I'll need a few example request-ids to find the exact edge trace.
jess-support: customer replied: removed prefetch and stream stayed stable. they can't disable prefetch in prod easily though. asking for server-side guard + doc for customers.
sam-frontend: note for docs: call out Safari prefetch + CDN 304 interaction, recommend SSE endpoints be non-cacheable and provide minimal server keepalive. add snippet:
```
// node express SSE example
res.set({
  'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-cache, no-transform',
  'Connection': 'keep-alive',
  'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no'
});
res.write(':connected\n\n');
setInterval(() => res.write(':keepalive\n\n'), 10000);
```
jess-support: customer asked if authentication via Authorization header is supported for EventSource — confirm yes but must ensure Vary: Authorization on responses and that CDN doesn't strip auth when generating cache keys.
leo-eng-sre: agreed. we'll push a short-lived CDN config change to exempt /v1/streams from caching and add an observability flag to detect 304s to SSE paths. deploy-bot: scheduled change for 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: cf:cache-rule-exempt /v1/streams deployed to staging at 2026-03-11T20:30Z :rocket:
jess-support: marking as high priority for customer enterprise account. asked them to send request-id and local repro timeline. will follow up once we have logs. :white_check_mark:
